one_line_pitch_to_sam: It's not a game, it's a test place on a baseplate: the sword fights look good and you take a nap when you die, but there's no sound, no kill counter and nothing to do.

moments.why: Spawning on a bare grey baseplate is the first thing they tell Sam, as proof it is not a real game.
The run looked clean in the moment but nothing happened with it, so it faded.
Crouch was declared useless in ten seconds and never came up again.
Remembered only as the tower with nothing on top where Kai wanted a chest.
The flailing arms were funny, but landing with no fall damage made it a one-time joke.
The pool was pleasant, had nothing at the bottom, and left no story to tell.
Sitting on the bench led to six seconds of silence and an 'ok'.
Punching air was just the first button press, overwritten by the sword.
Punching the dummy blurred into the general memory of jumping it.
Kai recalls that mashing gives a combo and that the fighting looks good, without specifics.
The kick was a brief discovery that the sword immediately made irrelevant.
Block survives only as 'there's a block button', since they never could tell if it worked.
Pressing 1 to equip is plumbing; they remember the sword, not drawing it.
The sword lunge is what made the fights good and what Robin calls broken.
The dummy lying down and popping back in their faces was a surprise, and Kai still knows it takes seven hits for nothing.
The first-to-five with a self-counted countdown and the spawn-kill argument is their main shared story.
The roll-over-and-nap death is the biggest laugh of the night and the only thing both call funny.
Robin remembers being invincible; Kai remembers it as boring to hit a silent wall.
Waving at the dummy got no reaction, so there was nothing to remember.
Dancing in total silence was a quick giggle that mostly sticks because of what happened next.
Working through the emote list was Robin ticking boxes while Kai waited.
Emotes that did nothing were a small confusion that got dropped.
Being slashed mid-dance and going straight from dancing to napping got a real laugh from both.
Robin remembers saying 'hello sir' to the creepy breathing guy before they realised it was a dummy.
Running to the void and realising the baseplate was the whole game was the big letdown.
No kill counter, score, sound or goal is the complaint they repeat most and the reason they quit.
